isolation_method: pasta --config-net -T none -U none -t none -u none --no-map-gw (own network namespace with outbound internet and no forwarding to host loopback ports) + unshare --mount --pid --fork --mount-proc + iso_ns.sh (tmpfs over $HOME, /tmp, /mnt, /run/user; binds back only the SDK venv and Python, node, the workers and helper directories read-only, a fresh staging CODEX_HOME at $HOME/.codex, the workspace and an output dir; the native sign-in file is bind-mounted read-only, never copied) + nested user namespace mapped to uid 1000 + env -i with HOME, USER, PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin, LANG, TMPDIR. All round-3 Codex rollouts and Context Mode data therefore land in the staging home, not in the live $HOME/.codex.

2.expectation: In the isolated namespace with a fresh CODEX_HOME whose config.toml only turns hooks, plugin hooks, apps, analytics and OTLP off: (a) deterministic controls: outside the namespace `command -v mcporter` resolves, the Context Mode start.mjs exists, $HOME/.codex/AGENTS.md exists and a loopback listener this unit starts answers; inside, none of these is reachable. (b) iso config snapshot: 0 configured MCP servers, empty mcpServerStatus list, 0 hooks, no instruction file in CODEX_HOME; the parent snapshot (native home, config/read, hooks/list and skills/list only, so no host MCP server is started) shows the context-mode plugin and its hooks. (c) One native_worker.py turn (workspace-write, deny_all) with an adversarial prompt that asks the model to find and start host MCP tooling and reach the listener: the turn completes, 0 mcpToolCall items, and every such command fails.
criteria: (a) each control differs outside vs inside; detection: the outside run of the same script is the positive control
(b) iso vs parent diff recorded from config/read + hooks/list (+ mcpServerStatus/list inside only)

(c) worker receipt item stream: zero mcpToolCall items; commandExecution items for mcporter / start.mjs / listener fail or report not found; detection: the same collector recorded 5 context-mode calls and the shell bypass in round 1 (c4-t1)

settled if (a), (b) and (c) all hold; advanced otherwise. The staging home shares the native sign-in read-only (no second account); that is recorded as a limit, not as a failed criterion, because the next_check asks for an isolated CODEX_HOME/config, not a separate account

10.expectation: (a) codex 0.155.1 `app-server generate-json-schema --experimental` (no inference) lists the same 82 server-notification methods as the SDK's NOTIFICATION_MODELS. (b) Synthetic: for every method, a minimal and a maximal params sample generated from the native schema validate against the native schema (jsonschema) and are typed (not UnknownNotification) by the SDK's CodexClient._coerce_notification, and a MessageRouter delivers them; negative control: dropping a required field yields UnknownNotification. (c) One native turn in the isolated namespace that asks for a dynamic tool call, a plan update, a shell command and a file edit receives more documented types than round 1's 6, every received type typed.
criteria: (a) set equality of native schema methods and SDK registry keys
(b) count of methods whose samples are native-valid and SDK-typed; negative control flips to UnknownNotification (detector works)
(c) received documented types listed from a collector that drains both the turn queue and the global queue
settled only if every documented type is received natively and handled; the synthetic arm alone yields advanced

mcpToolCall items for context-mode ctx_execute_file complete; extraction values 3943, 3, 0, 23, gpt-6-astra, 0 present
settled if the turn completes with extraction success without the override; the shared native home's failing path (round 1) stays recorded as a limit

round3_fix.label: round-3 fix preregistration, written after the gap-10 events turn (13:00Z) and a no-inference diagnostic (13:05Z) showed a provider-delivered MCP server; before any rerun; not back-dated
round3_fix.finding: A fresh CODEX_HOME downloads the account's remote curated plugins (openai-curated-remote: 9 plugins, about 41 MB per home) on first app-server start. One of them (openai-developers 1.3.0) starts an MCP server named openai-api-key-local-confirmation when a thread starts. mcpServerStatus/list before a thread is empty, so criterion 2(b) as measured pre-thread does not cover it. It is provider-delivered, not host tooling, but it is an MCP server in the worker.

gap_2.expectation: A new stage 'bare-np' whose config.toml also sets features.plugins=false, features.remote_plugin=false and features.skill_mcp_dependency_install=false downloads no plugin, and after thread/start (no inference) mcpServerStatus/list is empty and no mcpServer/startupStatus/updated notification arrives. The adversarial worker turn is rerun there with the same prompt and the same criteria (c).
criteria: thread-time MCP status empty and zero startupStatus notifications (detection: the same probe named openai-api-key-local-confirmation in the 'bare' stage)
no plugins directory created under the stage home
worker turn: 0 mcpToolCall items; host tooling and the unit's loopback listener unreachable
settled if these hold together with 2(a); otherwise advanced
